entityDescription:
The business vision of Automaton is about “Improving productivity and asset performance 
with automation”. 
In other words, we automate the machines our customers use. We do this by retrofitting 
our equipment to our customers' machines and making them remotely operable. 
Our solution consists of hardware and software components. The guidance of the 
equipment will be handled via Galileo HAS satellite guidance and OSNMA authorization. 
Our business model is based on a service model. Instead of one time equipment sale we 
provide a full service to our customers, including installation and continuous user support. 
Our pricing model is based on a monthly invoiced contract.
Our customers will not be required to make a sizable investment to install our equipment. 
It will be relatively low entry / low risk to opt for our service. 
AT 1 product i.e. our first and currently only product will be meant for heavy duty rollers 
which are used in construction sites to level the site and make the ground compact enough 
to build on (roads, construction sites etc). 
Our co-founders, Aapo, Tuomo, and Sami, bring to the table a perfect blend of technical 
expertise, business acumen, and practical experience. Aapo, with over a decade in 
automation and robotics entrepreneurship, provides the technical backbone, while 
Tuomo's years of experience in high-tech sales and delivery ensure a customer-centric 
approach. Sami, with his hands-on experience with various machines, adds invaluable 
practical insights to onsite installation and delivery of the equipment.
We're not just automating machines; we're constructing the future of work, brick by brick, 
one automated machine at a time. Welcome to Automaton, where innovation meets 
application.

Stiftelsen Seilskipet Statsraad Lehmkuhl is a nonprofit foundation primarily aims to preserve the sailing ship 'Statsraad Lehmkuhl' for future generations and provide it with a dignified purpose of use that aligns with the ship's tradition, including maritime vocational training. On 15th April 2023, the Norwegian tall ship, Statsraad Lehmkuhl, returned to Bergen from a 20- months circumnavigation of the globe during her “One Ocean Expedition 2021 – 2023”. The expedition is a recognized part of the UN´s Ocean Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development.The main goal of the expedition was to “create attention and share knowledge about the crucial role of the Ocean for a sustainable development in a global perspective”, and therein a special focus on SDG 14 and SDG 13. The expedition was also a brilliant showcase of SDG17 with a strong and dedicated partnership with more the 40 partners from public sector, education, research, innovation and commerce.
Wherever the ship sailed it created massive attention around the main goal. In ports, the ship served for conferences, receptions, high- level meetings and diplomacy. At sea, the ship served as a floating university, bringing on board students and scientists from all over the world to discuss and study Ocean matters. On board, everyone works together to sail the ship and gather experience and knowledge about the ocean and each other.
As part of the preparations to the expedition, the ship was equipped with state of the art research instruments, and the ship has since served as a sail training – and research vessel. More advanced research instruments and a new laboratory will be installed in 2024
